# tritonctl ssh-key

Manage SSH keys

Alias: key

Subcommands: list, show, create, delete

Usage: `tritonctl ssh-key [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>`

## tritonctl ssh-key list

List your SSH keys

Alias: ls

Usage: `tritonctl ssh-key list [OPTIONS]`

## tritonctl ssh-key show

Show one SSH key

Usage: `tritonctl ssh-key show [OPTIONS] <ID>`

- `<ID>`: Key name, fingerprint, uuid, or prefix

## tritonctl ssh-key create

Register a new SSH key owned by you

Usage: `tritonctl ssh-key create [OPTIONS] --name <NAME>`

- `--name <NAME>` (required)
- `--description <DESCRIPTION>`
- `--public-key <PUBLIC_KEY>`: OpenSSH-formatted public key string
- `--public-key-file <PUBLIC_KEY_FILE>`: Path to a file containing the OpenSSH public key

## tritonctl ssh-key delete

Delete an SSH key

Alias: rm

Usage: `tritonctl ssh-key delete [OPTIONS] <ID>`

- `<ID>`: Key name, fingerprint, uuid, or prefix
- `-n, --dry-run`: Print what would change and stop
- `-y, --yes`: Answer yes to the confirmation. The summary still prints
- `--keep-going`: Keep executing after a step fails
